newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines cuts power rates in four of five grids.
newsitem.headline: Philippines cuts power rates in four of five grids.

text.p: The Philippines' National Power Corp (Napocor) reduced on Monday power rates by 1.28 centavos per kilowatt-hour (kwh) in the main northern island of Luzon.
The state-run Napocor said that customers in the Luzon grid will now pay 2.3144 pesos per kwh from the previous rate of 2.3272 pesos.

In the central Philippines, power rates in the Leyte-Samar grid were reduced by 1.67 centavos per kwh and by 0.92 centavos in the Bohol grid. In the southern Mindanao region, power rates were reduced by 0.60 centavos per kwh.
Only rates in the Cebu-Negros-Panay grids in central Philippines were raised by a minimal 0.14 centavos per kwh.

Napocor said the reduction was brought about by improvement in the heat rates of power plants, a measure of their increased efficiency, despite the higher cost of power bought from privately-operated power facilities.
The appreciation of the peso versus the U.S. dollar and the yen also led to the downward adjustment, the power firm added.
The adjustments will cover the period January 26 up to February 25. - Manila newsroom 63 2 8418939 fax 8176267
